concerns.location: spec.md:User Story 1 - Automated Comment Generation and Dataset Preparation
concerns.text: User Story 1 has functional requirements (FR‑001, FR‑002) but no Success Criteria are anchored to it. All SC‑### entries reference US‑2 or US‑3; none mention US‑1, leaving the story without measurable outcomes.

Cross‑reference to user stories uses the identifier ‘US-1’, ‘US-2’, ‘US-3’ (e.g., “(See US-1)”), but the user stories are labeled as ‘User Story 1’, ‘User Story 2’, ‘User Story 3’ in the document. This mismatch makes the reference ambiguous and breaks traceability.

FR-006 states the system MUST validate the availability and relevance of the data collection environment and participant recruitment tools before the user study begins, but provides no concrete, observable criteria or test procedure to verify this validation.

The edge‑case handling for code snippets that exceed the model’s context window says the system MUST truncate to a predefined maximum token limit, yet the actual token limit value is not specified, making the behavior untestable.

The specification replaces the idea’s plan to use the existing CodeSearchNet developer‑comprehension benchmark (≈50 tasks) with a *new controlled user study* (US‑3). This changes the experimental methodology and introduces a different source of human performance data, effectively redefining the research approach without justification. The idea’s research question remains the same, but the way it will be answered has been altered, constituting a drift in scope.

concerns.location: spec.md:User Story 3 - Statistical Analysis and Hypothesis Testing
concerns.text: The current design assigns each code snippet to a single comment condition (LLM, human, or none) and randomizes participants to a single condition for the entire study. This conflates snippet difficulty with comment type, creating a confound that prevents causal attribution of performance differences to the comment condition. A valid causal inference requires either (a) each snippet being evaluated under all three conditions (within‑subject or counterbalanced across participants) or (b) a fully crossed, balanced between‑subjects design with multiple participants per snippet per condition.
